items.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001
items.q: I think what that comes from is playing with Billy and Bud Powell

ctx.x: Jane Jarvis says that you have this amazing ability to pick the right notes as the chords progress and it would depend on whether this is a passing chord. She just is amazed at your ability.

I thank her for that. I think what that comes from is playing with Billy and Bud Powell and playing with a lot of other people that I’ve played with. It comes from, especially with Billy. Because Billy would play things just to really see if he could fool me, to see if I couldn’t find the bass. Nine times out of ten I would find the right note in the chord. And he says that’s something that you either have it or you don’t. I don’t know how true that is. But she — when I play with her, especially if we’re in a…
Well you’ve come a long way since the violin. You did some work with the “Sophisticated Lady” show.
